claims.text: Premelting in CrMnFeNiCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is primarily governed by local lattice strain induced by atomic-size mismatch.
Local lattice strain reduces local cohesive energies.
Reduced local cohesive energy lowers the onset temperature of melting.
Local lattice strain broadens the melting transition.
The baseline nanoparticles are equiatomic CrMnFeNiCu particles with diameters from 5 to 20 nm.
Equiatomic CrMnFeNiCu has minimal atomic-size variance and correspondingly low local lattice strain and defect density.
Substituting one or two constituent elements can increase atomic-size differences relative to the equiatomic CrMnFeNiCu baseline.
Increasing atomic-size mismatch increases local lattice strain and associated defect density.
Strain fields and defect sites lower local binding energy and facilitate atomic mobility at lower temperatures.
Nanoparticles with greater atomic-size mismatch will have a lower premelting onset temperature than the baseline nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with greater atomic-size mismatch will have a broader and more gradual melting transition than the baseline nanoparticles.
Measured local lattice strain should correlate with the magnitude of melting-temperature depression.
The proposed mechanism should hold for nanoparticles from 5 to 20 nm when heated under an inert atmosphere.
Outside the 5–20 nm range or under reactive atmospheres, additional effects may alter melting behavior.
Changes in mixing enthalpy or other compositional variables may contribute to the observed melting behavior.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that compositional substitution will ensure that only atomic-size-attributable strain is altered, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that the substitution may also change mixing enthalpy and other compositional variables.
